title: Prove D1^4 = I leaves the residual x1 monomial nonzero
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Change and mathematical scope

Scoped proof. No new κ. The selected conditional value stays `781451/250000000` from the selected record (PR #6030). This does not change the selected frontier.

The formal algebra of the published two-edge feed imposes `Q^4 = C1^2 = C3^2 = I` and the inherited rule that `D_i` conjugates only `C_i` by `Q^{-1}`. One physical relation omitted by that algebra is the fresh-Gaussian equation `D1^4 = I`. In the quotient by that single central equation, the residual word

```text
Q^{-1} C1 Q^2 C1 C3 D1 D3
```

keeps the representative with word `(-1, 2, 1, 1, 2, 3)` and degree `(1, 1)`, coefficient 1. The comparison element `Q^{-1} C1` keeps the distinct representative with word `(-1, 2)` and degree `(0, 0)`. The Q-letter parity character still sends that representative to `-1`.

Evidence class: a proof that one named central group relation does not send one explicit monomial to zero. The quotient is the predecessor group algebra modulo `(D1^4 - 1)`. This is not a word census, not a bounded search, and not a theorem that the monomial survives every physical relation at once. `D3^4 = I` is not imposed. The 8-dimensional separating representation also satisfies `D3^4 = I` and `(C1 C3)^3 = I`; those are extra relations of the matrices, labelled as such. No autonomous caller is exhibited.

## Task and overlap

Base: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`. Task: `joint-query-controller`, scope refined. This answers open question 2 of open PR #7033: name one source relation outside `Q^4 = C1^2 = C3^2 = I` and the inherited D conjugation rule, then reduce only the residual word. It does not redo the D-exponent-0 obstruction and does not take the nonzero D-exponent question.

Overlap snapshot on 2026-11-10, via `scripts/find_overlap.py`: local notes at that base (10178 paths, complete inventory), 339 open-PR records fetched at 10:19:05Z, and 7013 discussion records fetched at 10:20:14Z. The phrase `Q^{-1} C1 Q^2 C1 C3` matches #7033 and discussion comment 19513867, which ask this question. Requiring both `physical relation` and `D^4`, and both `omitted` and `D^4=I`, matched nothing in that snapshot. The search is not a novelty certificate. Closed PR bodies were outside that snapshot.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only. From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/residual-d1-fourth-power --check-only
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/residual-d1-fourth-power
```

Both registered commands passed locally, including the optimized run. Checks are explicit `need` failures, not assertions. The run prints `PASS_RESIDUAL_D1_FOURTH_POWER` and `new_kappa null`.

Not run: the native eight-axis Gaussian word, `D3^4 = I` as a formal quotient, any linear relation in `Q, C1, C3`, nonzero D exponents, and any owner-indexed multiplier.

## Credit

The trace, algebra, and omitted-relation sentence are Cinna Davis's `research/coded-active-feedback`, using Dugongue's PR4948 chronology, Dillon's PR4933 code, and `research/coded-native-caller/gauge.py`. The normalized one-axis law `D^2 = X`, `D^4 = I` is Nick Petalas's `research/moving-stage-restoration-tariff`. The residual monomial is the open remainder of the D-exponent-0 x1 obstruction (PR #7033).

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance.

## Open next questions

The package records two follow-ups.

Does one linear source relation, compatible with `Q^4 = C1^2 = C3^2 = I` and the inherited D conjugation rule, send the coefficient word `Q^{-1} C1 Q^2 C1 C3` to zero while leaving `Q^{-1} C1` nonzero? The first step is to evaluate `C = diag(K_i)^{-1} F diag(K_i)` from `research/native-involutive-dual/PROOF.md` on one shared central axis and reduce that coefficient. `D1^4 = I` cannot, because the coefficient has D degree `(0, 0)`.

If a later quotient does send the residual to zero and keeps `Q^{-1} C1` nonzero, which owner-indexed multiplier on the four published banks becomes the autonomous row `[A, 0, 0, 0]`? The first step is to name that quotient and recompute the four columns. No such quotient is constructed here.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The omitted relation named by the predecessor is a central group equation, so the coset sum of one monomial decides it. A word search would not see that the class stays nonzero. Link once: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200
